record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: When AIXI is specialized to a sequence-prediction task, does it predict sequences as well as Solomonoff’s universal prediction scheme even though AIXI does not literally reduce to Solomonoff prediction and the universal prior M is defined on inputs rather than directly on outputs?

evidence.quote: l) Using AIXI for prediction. Since AIXI is a unification of sequential decision theory with the idea of universal probability one may think that the AIXI model for a sequence prediction problem exactly reduces to Solomonoff’s universal sequence prediction scheme. Unfortunately this is not the case. ... The questions is whether, nevertheless, AIXI predicts sequences as well as Solomonoff’s scheme.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Fix a finite alphabet of observations $\mathcal{O}$, a finite alphabet of actions $\mathcal{A}$, and a finite alphabet of rewards $\mathcal{R}\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Let $U$ be a fixed universal monotone Turing machine, and define Solomonoff's universal semimeasure on input strings by
$$M(x)\;=\;\sum_{p:\;U(p)=x*}2^{-\ell(p)},$$
where the sum runs over minimal programs $p$ that, when fed to $U$, output a string having $x\in(\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{R})^{*}$ as a prefix, and $\ell(p)$ is the length of $p$ in bits.

Solomonoff's universal predictor. For sequences $z_{1:\infty}\in\mathcal{O}^{\infty}$ generated by an unknown computable measure $\mu$, Solomonoff's universal sequence prediction scheme predicts $z_{n+1}$ from $z_{1:n}$ using the conditional
$$M_{\mathrm{seq}}(z_{n+1}\mid z_{1:n})\;=\;\frac{M_{\mathrm{seq}}(z_{1:n+1})}{M_{\mathrm{seq}}(z_{1:n})},$$
where $M_{\mathrm{seq}}$ is the universal semimeasure defined directly on output sequences.

AIXI. The AIXI agent at time $n$, having observed history $h_{<n}=a_1 o_1 r_1\cdots a_{n-1}o_{n-1}r_{n-1}$, chooses
$$a_n^{\mathrm{AIXI}}\;=\;\arg\max_{a_n}\sum_{o_n r_n}\!\cdots\!\max_{a_m}\sum_{o_m r_m}\!\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_{k=n}^{m}r_k\Bigr)\,M(o_1 r_1\cdots o_m r_m\mid a_1\cdots a_m),$$
for a finite horizon $m$, where $M$ is conditioned on the action sequence (actions are inputs, not predicted by $M$).

Prediction specialization. Specialize AIXI to a pure sequence-prediction task: the agent must output a guess $\hat z_n\in\mathcal{O}$ for the next symbol $z_n$ of an unknown computable sequence and receives reward $r_n=1$ iff $\hat z_n=z_n$ (and $0$ otherwise). Identify $a_n$ with $\hat z_n$ and $o_n r_n$ with $(z_n,\mathbb{1}[\hat z_n=z_n])$.

Question. Even though, in this specialization, AIXI does not literally reduce to Solomonoff's universal sequence prediction scheme—because $M$ is the universal semimeasure on input/interaction strings rather than directly on output sequences—does the AIXI policy nonetheless achieve sequence-prediction performance comparable to Solomonoff's universal predictor? Concretely: prove or disprove that for every computable measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{O}^{\infty}$, the expected number of prediction errors made by AIXI on $\mu$-distributed sequences is finite (or bounded by a constant multiple of the corresponding bound for Solomonoff's scheme), and quantify any loss in performance relative to Solomonoff prediction.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether AIXI, when specialized to sequence prediction, performs as well as Solomonoff's universal predictor was raised as an open problem in the universal induction/AIXI literature. Subsequent work on AIXI (computability, optimality variants, AIXI^tl, limit-computable approximations) does not appear to have settled this specific equivalence/comparison question. No source found in the search explicitly resolves it, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Universal Algorithmic Intelligence (Hutter)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses AIXI and Solomonoff induction; notes AIXI does not reduce to Solomonoff prediction in the sequence-prediction case.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between AIXI specialized to prediction and Solomonoff prediction is discussed but not formally resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the computability of Solomonoff induction and AIXI
status_evidence.snippet: Studies computability properties of AIXI and Solomonoff induction in the arithmetical hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on AIXI focuses on computability rather than the prediction-equivalence question, which is not addressed as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Principles of Solomonoff Induction and AIXI
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style account of AIXI and Solomonoff induction.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys do not report a proof that AIXI matches Solomonoff prediction performance in the sequence-prediction specialization.
